fact: AlgerieZoom reports that the DGI's Jibayatic tele-declaration and tele-payment system, in which only large-enterprise (DGE) taxpayers were previously required to file electronically, is generalised to all local tax structures under DGI instruction 31/2026 of 6 May 2026.
AlgerieZoom reports that taxpayers of tax centres, proximity centres and inspections can pay taxes remotely through Jibayatic for the first time, as an optional method.

AlgerieZoom reports that electronic filing is mandatory for DGE taxpayers and, under instruction 31/2026, for real-profit regime and simplified non-commercial-profession taxpayers, though 2025 returns other than series G n°50 may still be filed on paper.
The DGI guide says taxes, duties and levies declared online on the Jibaya'tic portal can be paid online.
The DGI guide says online payment via Jibaya'tic by bank transfer or CIB/Edahabia card is available for declared obligations.
The DGI says Jibayatic users get online tax declaration (teledeclaration) and teleparment services.
The DGI says taxes can be paid remotely via Jibayatic by CIB, Edahabia or bank transfer.

The 2026 Finance Law requires real-regime taxpayers in IT-equipped tax services to file returns electronically, and wealth-tax filers to file through the DGI information system's automated calculation.
The booklet says real-regime taxpayers may settle taxes and duties electronically, and IFU taxpayers may file and pay electronically, in IT-equipped tax services.
The 2026 Finance Law makes electronic filing mandatory for real-regime taxpayers, G29 payroll declarations and wealth tax filers under DGI-equipped tax offices.
